solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Servant that’s packing a vessel in Kyrgyzstan

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so the country code holds the other pieces within it

blocks.note: KS is the international vehicle registration code for Kyrgyzstan
taken as written
a vas is a vessel or duct in the body

explanation.surface: A household servant carries a pot or jug around Kyrgyzstan.
explanation.definitionFit: A kavass is an armed attendant or constable serving officials in Turkey, a kind of servant.

clue.text: King approved a letter

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
app. is a standard abbreviation of approved
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch gives his approval to a piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a letter' looks like a document the king approved; the 'a' is shared out, since it is the last piece and the definition is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is one letter.

clue.text: Occupy oneself with once filling glass of Champagne very quickly

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so the first piece goes into the second

blocks.note: verre is French for glass, and Champagne is a French region
entreat is an obsolete verb meaning to treat of or occupy oneself with something

explanation.surface: Someone once busied themselves with pouring a glass of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: Champagne with a capital letter is the region, which tells the solver to work in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventre à terre is a French phrase, belly to the ground, describing a horse at full gallop, hence at top speed.

clue.text: Toil locally in Seychelles, enduring great heat

indicators.note: in places the toil word inside the code for the island country

blocks.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
tew is a dialect word meaning to work hard

explanation.surface: Labourers in the Seychelles put up with sweltering temperatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewy describes being hot and stuffy, like food left simmering in a pot, so close and oppressive.

clue.text: Has already moved enclosure for lots of animals?

indicators.note: moved means shifted out of place, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: has can be shortened to 's, as in he's done it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has already relocated a pen for many animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that lots are auction lots, not simply many animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A saleyard is a pen or yard where livestock are kept and auctioned in lots, chiefly an Australian term.

clue.text: In places rain brought up English iris

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lis is the heraldic iris, as in fleur-de-lis

explanation.surface: In some places wet weather made the English iris grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In places' is not a container signal: it marks the definition as a regional word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sile is a dialect verb for pouring or raining heavily, used only in some parts of the country.

clue.text: Russian measure formerly linked to volume

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for volume
erst is an archaic word for formerly

explanation.surface: A Russian unit of measurement used to be tied to volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A verst is an old Russian unit of distance of about two thirds of a mile.

clue.text: Scottish readers just of poetry

blocks.note: first meaning: eyes, in Scots, since eyes are what you read with
second meaning: the poetic contraction of even, in the sense of just or exactly

explanation.walkthrough: Readers are not people reading but the organs doing it; just is an adverb, not fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Een is the Scots plural of eye, and e'en is the contracted poetic spelling of even, meaning just.

clue.text: True about Greek character chasing money, flowing under the bridge?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for true goes around the Greek letter
chasing means running behind, so this part comes after the money in a down clue

blocks.note: rhino is old slang for money
true and real are synonyms
rho is the Greek letter R

explanation.surface: A sincere account of a Greek following the money, like water under the bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is the bridge of the nose, not one over a river; the idiom about water under the bridge is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinorrhoea is a runny nose, so rhinorrhoeal describes mucus running beneath the nasal bridge.

clue.text: Gliding condors flying around both ends of range

indicators.note: both ends of keeps only the first and last letters of the following word
flying suggests scattering through the air, so these letters are rearranged
around means encircling, so the rearranged birds surround the selected pair

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of range

explanation.surface: Condors soar on the wind over a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gliding' reads as describing the condors, but it is the definition, an Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorrendo is a musical instruction meaning sliding or flowing smoothly from note to note.

clue.text: Awards working within limits

indicators.note: within means inside, so the word for working sits inside the word for limits

blocks.note: a tie is a bond or restriction that limits someone
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Prizes given for work done under constraints.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonies are Tony awards, the annual American prizes for achievement in Broadway theatre.

clue.text: A venerable lower part to finish off casque?

definitions.text: A venerable lower part to finish off casque?

indicators.note: finish off points to the final letter only of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
Ven. is the abbreviated title for Venerable, as for an archdeacon
the tail is the lower or hind part of something
the final letter of casque

explanation.surface: An old helmet gets a time-honoured lower flap to complete it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a casque is a helmet, and this piece of armour hangs from its lower edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An aventaile is the movable mail flap or visor attached to the lower part of a medieval helmet.

clue.text: Criticise uproar involved in one council

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
hell can mean chaos or uproar, as in all hell broke loose
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slams a commotion that one council member was caught up in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' looks like a container, but 'in one' is the material that gets rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panhellenion was an assembly representing all Greek cities, established under Emperor Hadrian.

clue.text: Past tense — that of place up north

blocks.note: pa. t. is the dictionary abbreviation for past tense

explanation.surface: A grammar note explaining a verb's past form as used in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots pit means put or place; that is the place up north, and this is its past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists this as the Scots past tense of pit, the northern dialect verb meaning to put.

clue.text: Unpaid debt locally, it runs back over time

blocks.note: arrear is an old and dialect adverb meaning behind or backward, as of payments running late
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A debt nobody pays keeps rolling back over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrearage is money owed and overdue, the state of being behind with payments.

clue.text: Lazy Scots son getting little right

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
wee means little
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An idle Scottish boy is given only a small amount of what is due.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweert is a Scots adjective meaning reluctant or slothful, unwilling to work.

clue.text: Serial sure to be broadcast about Detective Sergeant

indicators.note: to be broadcast suggests scattering widely, so the letters of sure are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged word goes around the police rank

blocks.note: taken as written
DS is the abbreviation for Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A TV series about a police detective is bound to be aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudser is American slang for a soap opera, a long-running dramatic serial.

clue.text: Sheep so much getting over hail

blocks.note: the can mean so much or by that amount, as in so much the better
ave is the Latin greeting hail

explanation.surface: A sheep suffers badly in a storm of hailstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A theave is a young ewe, especially one in its first or second year.

clue.text: Fight large number in US street to protect girlfriend

indicators.note: to protect is to shield by surrounding, so the large number goes around the girlfriend

blocks.note: slue is an American spelling of slew, a large number
GF is the abbreviation for girlfriend
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A crowd in an American street steps in to shield a young woman during a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is a fight full of heavy blows, an American slang term for a brawl.

clue.text: Supporter upset about Hearts

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for upset goes around the card suit

blocks.note: sore means upset or aggrieved
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A football fan is annoyed about Hearts, the Edinburgh club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like a reversal signal but means aggrieved; Hearts is Heart of Midlothian, a Scottish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A shore is a prop or beam set against a wall or ship to support it.

clue.text: Declared once that only half must go

indicators.note: only half must go tells the solver to remove half the letters of the word, keeping the rest

blocks.note: the clue's first word serves again as the source

explanation.surface: Someone once announced that just half was to be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word does double duty: drop the first half of declared and its second half is the archaic past tense of arede.
explanation.definitionFit: Ared is the old past tense of arede, an obsolete verb meaning to declare, explain or counsel.

clue.text: Endlessly heartless tangling fly’s wings?

indicators.note: endlessly means without an ending, so the last letter is dropped
tangling means twisting together, so the letters are muddled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel person keeps snarling up a fly's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits these are not true wings but organs that evolved from them.
explanation.definitionFit: Halteres are the small knobbed balancing organs of flies, evolved from the hind pair of wings.

clue.text: Wave brushes a coral

indicators.note: wave as an imperative means to wave something about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wave sweeps over a coral reef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like the sea, which is the scene; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Some branching corals such as sea fans grow like bushy plants on the seabed, hence the name sea shrub.

clue.text: Society has legal distraint over feudal tenant

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the legal word reads upwards

blocks.note: Soc. is the abbreviation for society
nam is an old legal term for distraint, the seizure of goods

explanation.surface: A society has goods seized by law from a feudal tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A socman held land by socage, a medieval tenure paid by service or rent rather than military duty.

clue.text: Water buffalo Albanian’s not allowed out

indicators.note: not allowed means barred, so the following word is removed from the soldier

blocks.note: an Arnaout is an Albanian, especially an Albanian soldier in Turkish service
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Albanian is banned from letting the water buffalo out.
explanation.definitionFit: The arna is the wild Asian water buffalo of India, the ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.

clue.text: Western? Linking this with Florida would be a blunder

indicators.note: linking this with means the answer plus another piece makes a longer word, so that piece is taken away from it

blocks.note: a floater is slang for a blunder or gaffe
FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: Combining a cowboy film with a Florida setting would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: the answer with the state added makes the blunder, so take the state off.
explanation.definitionFit: An oater is American slang for a cowboy film, from the oats fed to the horses.

clue.text: Bleak Scottish housing temperature? A little awkward for locals

indicators.note: housing means giving shelter to, so the Scots word holds the temperature abbreviation inside

blocks.note: blae is a Scots word for bleak or livid in colour
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A cold Scottish house with an uncertain temperature makes the locals slightly uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Blate is a Scots and northern dialect word for bashful or shy, socially a bit awkward.

clue.text: Fellow embracing hot mate once

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the word for fellow surrounds the abbreviation

blocks.note: a peer is an equal or fellow
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man hugs his hot old partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheer, also spelt fere, is an archaic word for a companion or spouse.

clue.text: Rapidly flick through, upset about following pages

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for upset goes around the abbreviation

blocks.note: to rile is to annoy or upset
ff. is the abbreviation for and the following pages

explanation.surface: Someone thumbs quickly through a book, irritated by what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: To riffle is to leaf quickly through pages, as one does when shuffling cards.

clue.text: Following my growth in part of Spain

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following
lor is a colloquial exclamation like my, a form of Lord

explanation.surface: Following my own development in a region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Flor is the film of yeast that grows on the surface of sherry in Jerez, in southern Spain.

clue.text: My chimney-cowl turns endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means losing the end, so the final letter is dropped
turns means facing about, so the remaining letters read backwards

blocks.note: a hood is a cowl over a chimney

explanation.surface: My cowl on the chimney keeps spinning round in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive in the surface but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations expressing surprise or delight, as in my, how lovely or ooh, how lovely.

clue.text: Plant family does damage in the small intestine? Beware if taken regularly

indicators.note: taken regularly means picked at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: to mar is to damage, so mars means does damage
ileac means relating to the ileum, part of the small intestine
the second, fourth and sixth letters of beware

explanation.surface: A plant family harms the gut, so watch out if you eat it often.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsileaceae is the botanical family of water clover ferns, named after the genus Marsilea.

clue.text: Casually speaks English in southern Zambia

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the pair formed by the other two

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
E is the abbreviation for English
Z is the international vehicle registration code for Zambia

explanation.surface: Someone talks English informally in the south of Zambia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sez is a colloquial written spelling of says, imitating relaxed speech.

clue.text: Love restaurant and leave finally without a bill

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
the final letter of leave

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a romantic meal out and walks off without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill is a bird's beak, not a restaurant check.
explanation.definitionFit: Erostrate is a botanical and zoological term meaning beakless, lacking a beak or rostrum.

clue.text: See Z in N rotated? It emerges instinctively

indicators.note: in places the spelt-out last letter inside the spelt-out N
rotated means turned around, so the combined letters read backwards

blocks.note: en is the name of the letter N
zee is the American name of the letter Z

explanation.surface: Look: turn an N on its side and you get a Z, as if by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface tempts the solver to turn the letter shapes; instead spell the letters out as words.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeze is an old word for sneeze, an involuntary reflex that bursts out without thought.

clue.text: Sapling entirely covered in rot as seen from behind

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped around, so the word for rot surrounds the word for entirely
as seen from behind means viewed from the back, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: to ret is to soak flax so that it rots
all can mean entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A young tree is completely wrapped in decay when viewed from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellar, a variant of tiller, is a young tree or shoot springing from a stool or stump.
